neighbours.label: the hyphenated '-so' in the ironic hedge 'not-so-X' ('a not-so-quiet evening'), as against unhyphenated 'not so', 'so-so' and other uses of so
fire: The ad made a not-so-subtle jab at its biggest rival.
We spent a not-so-relaxing week at the beach with four toddlers.
The sequel offers a not-so-happy ending for its hero.
My cousin gave a not-so-brief speech at the wedding.
They moved into a not-so-quiet apartment above a bar.
Critics called it a not-so-clever remake of the original.
The diet promised quick results with some not-so-pleasant side effects.
Here is my list of the best and not-so-great pizza places in town.
quiet: The ad was not so subtle in its jab at its biggest rival.
We spent a very relaxing week at the beach with four toddlers.
The sequel offers a so-so ending for its hero.
My cousin gave such a brief speech at the wedding.
They moved into a so-called quiet apartment above a bar.
Critics called it a clever remake, and so did the fans.
The diet promised quick results, and so far it has worked.
Here is my list of the best and the worst pizza places in town.

predictions: fire 0.6-0.8 on '-so' after 'not'; 'not so' unhyphenated, 'so-so' and 'so' as an intensifier below 0.1
